hub.question: What free debate tools can I use without an account?
hub.answer: Four, all free and all usable without signing up: a round timer that knows the speech order and times of seven formats, a motion generator that draws from {{total}} original practice motions, a printable flow sheet with a column for every speech, and a speech time calculator. They run in your browser and save your rounds and drafts there, not on a server.

timer.question: Is there a free debate timer that knows each format's speech times?
timer.answer: Yes, this one. Pick Public Forum, Lincoln-Douglas, Policy, British Parliamentary, World Schools, Asian Parliamentary or the school 4-6-6-3 format, and it loads the speech order and lengths, shows the protected time when points of information are not allowed, and gives each side a prep bank in Public Forum, Lincoln-Douglas and Policy. It is free, needs no account, and keeps a running round through a page reload.

motions.question: Where can I get random debate motions for practice?
motions.answer: Draw them here. The generator picks one motion, or three for a veto drill, from {{total}} original practice motions written for this site, filtered by topic, difficulty and motion type, in This House or Resolved wording. It is free, needs no account, and lists every motion by topic further down the page.

flow.question: How do I make a debate flow sheet?
flow.answer: Choose your format and paper size here, then print. The sheet has a column for every speech in speaking order, labelled by speaker and coloured by side, and a strip along the bottom for cross-examination or point-of-information notes. For a PDF, choose Save as PDF in the print dialog. It is free and needs no account.

calc.question: How long will my speech take to deliver?
calc.answer: Divide its word count by your speaking rate. At an average 130 words per minute, a 520-word speech takes about 4 minutes; at a fast 160, about 3 minutes 15 seconds. Paste the speech into the calculator below to get the time at slow, average, fast and your own pace, and to see which debate speech slots it fits. The text never leaves your browser.
